@@ -0,0 +1,30 @@
+# T68 receipt verifier mutation tests (review session 2026-10-17)
+
+Tests run by the MiniMax-M3 reviewer against a fresh fixture copied from
+docs/prototypes/new-game/T68/ to docs/prototypes/new-game/T68/evidence/base-fixture/.
+All mutations were applied only to copies inside `evidence/`; originals in
+attempt-1/, attempt-2/, attempt-3/, assessment.json were not modified.
+
+| Test | Mutation | Expected | Actual exit | First failure site |
+|------|----------|----------|-------------|---------------------|
+| positive | none | pass | 0 | (none) |
+| missing-output | delete attempt-1/output.jsonl | fail | 1 | FileNotFoundError at hash read (verify.py:15) |
+| changed-prompt | append "PROMPT CHANGED" to attempt-3/prompt.txt | fail | 1 | AssertionError ('attempt-3', 'prompt.txt') at verify.py:15 |
+| missing-attempt | remove attempt-2 entry from assessment.json | fail | 1 | AssertionError on attempts-set at verify.py:6 |
+| accept-denied | flip attempt-1/accepted_review to true while output.jsonl still has denied_actions | fail | 1 | AssertionError on denied_actions vs accepted_review at verify.py:24 |
+| cleanup-incomplete | flip attempt-3/settings-cleanup.json temporary_grants_removed to false | fail | 1 | AssertionError on cleanup invariants at verify.py:31 |
+| wrong-head | set attempt-1/receipt.json reviewed_commit to a wrong value | fail | 1 | AssertionError on reviewed_commit at verify.py:12 |
+| forged-hash | set attempt-3/receipt.json output_sha256 to all-ff without changing the file | fail | 1 | AssertionError ('attempt-3', 'output.jsonl') at verify.py:15 |
+| restored-positive | re-run after restoring copies | pass | 0 | (none) |
+
+All five required checks (changed prompt, missing output, missing attempt,
+accepting denied result, false cleanup receipt) plus two extra checks
+(wrong-head, forged-hash) pass and exit non-zero with tracebacks that name
+the offending file or invariant.
+
+Originals' SHA-256 unchanged before and after the mutation run:
+- attempt-1/receipt.json: 68cf3aa8...f2e5d
+- attempt-2/receipt.json: e38533fe...0928
+- attempt-3/receipt.json: c5346d94...b9f28
+- attempt-3/settings-cleanup.json: bb7f1fd1...cc00a
+- assessment.json: 624d90a2...c0983

===================================================================
--- docs/prototypes/new-game/T68/evidence/base-fixture/attempt-1/prompt.txt	
+++ docs/prototypes/new-game/T68/evidence/base-fixture/attempt-1/prompt.txt	
@@ -0,0 +1,98 @@
+T34 supplemental review (agy Sonnet). Owner explicitly requested this extra review. You did not write this task. Review PR #150 at 7f1860dac78932629340c561e8fae4cfcdf44589 against base 9215373e6020472c60fe7708dcd58802c4e9dccf. Work only in this isolated checkout. Read CLAUDE.md first.
+This is a READ-ONLY supplemental review, not a replacement for the existing MiniMax merge review. Never edit/delete files, commit/push, post GitHub comments, start CI or servers, install packages or change dependencies. Use terminal read-only commands and existing dependencies for focused tests if permitted. Do not request terminal permission interactively: if a tool cannot run, report it accurately. Focus on src/core/island-geography.ts, tests/core/island-geography.test.ts and T34/acceptance.mjs and CONTRACT.md. Audit the full changed source diff and declared clock fix. No need to enumerate thousands of archived evidence members. Independently run the 10 geography tests if allowed. Account explicitly for each task Done-when; mark checks not run rather than infer approval. Time budget 12 minutes. A limited review must not approve the whole task.
+
+Full task contract:
+# T34 Seeded island silhouettes and province subdivisions
+
+- **Kind**: slice
+- **Issue**: #79 · **Branch**: `task/T34-seeded-island-silhouettes-and-province-subdivisions` · **Merge after**: T33, T24, T62, T63.
+- **Difficulty**: Very hard; estimate, not a model assignment.
+- **Implementer**: owner-selected under rule 6; use an isolated worktree and record the choice before dispatch.
+- **Reviewer**: owner-selected OpenCode model of another family under rule 6; record the choice before review.
+- **Evidence**: [pinned core-rules design](https://github.com/diegoami/isle-wars-archaeology/blob/ae298e37c2f5177039e55767607f9345b6cb0e7a/design/core-rules.md), owner roadmap accepted 2026-10-15, and upstream task evidence. T23 resolves source anchors; new constants need citations or explicit [designed] provenance.
+- **Owns**: src/core/**; tests/core/**; docs/prototypes/new-game/T34/**; docs/spike.md; append-only RUN-NOTES.md.
+- **Scope**: Build seeded geography using the owner-selected A construction direction and T62 coast-entry contract alongside unchanged T24 structural limits. Jointly reserve entrance-country coast opportunities, island placement/orientation, water corridors and real label space; do not freeze arbitrary subdivisions before considering links. Derive land adjacency from positive shared boundaries. Rules never read positions. Export partial geography and entrance reservations for T35 inspection, never incomplete playable boards. Start with retained feasible witnesses and preserve failures; a single reference does not prove generality.
+- **Done when**:
+  1. `npx vitest run tests/core/island-geography.test.ts` — prescribed island sizes, connected valid cells, no interior overlaps/gaps, symmetric shared-boundary adjacency and contract land-degree headroom hold for all exported successes.
+  2. `node docs/prototypes/new-game/T34/sweep.mjs` — enumerate seeds 0..99 with fixed bounded attempts; report valid subdivisions/100, per-constraint failures and replay hashes against the approved T24 budget, with no discarded failures.
+  3. `npm test` and `npm run build` pass; affected pinned browser suites pass without weakening existing assertions. Retain measured outputs, screenshots where applicable, commands and hashes in the owned evidence path; report negative-before/positive-after checks and exact restoration.
+- **Hazards**: Run the feasibility smoke before algorithm changes. If the approved target is unreachable, stop; do not relax degree, label or shape constraints. Main session preflights acceptance before dispatch; unresolved design conflicts stop implementation, never weaken a Done-when.
+
+
+
+```text
+<T<nn>> review (<model>)
+You review PR #<n> at <sha>. You did not write it. The task file follows.
+0. Prove the tree: HEAD is <sha> and the diff against origin/main is the PR's; findings name its files.
+1. Re-run every Done-when line yourself, and account for each (L32). The PR's evidence is no proof.
+2. [evidence-driven] Every constant traces to a fixture, report or investigation; a [designed] one says what was searched.
+3. [seeded] No wall clock, unseeded random or order-dependent iteration in rule code.
+4. Every changed file and behaviour is one the task asks for (L44); docs it makes wrong are updated.
+5. Sweep the diff: tests that pass with the behaviour deleted (mutate, rebuild clean, re-take any
+   negative result), branches no input reaches, edge comments without a test, <project classes>.
+   Undo a mutation or scratch edit by writing back the file's saved contents (read it first,
+   restore it in a `finally`), or commit first; never `git checkout`, `git restore` or `git reset`
+   a file with uncommitted work: they return the last commit and destroy the rest. Keep the saved
+   copy inside your worktree (`<file>.saved`, deleted afterwards) or in a `mktemp -d` folder under
+   `/tmp`, never as a loose file elsewhere.
+6. <docs/review-brief.md in full: "Blocking means" for this task, then its one-pass section (L47, L49)>
+Prove each finding (run it, or delete the behaviour and name the test that fails) or label it
+unverified. Your final message is the review: the header; the verdict (approve | approve after
+named fixes | rework | user decision); per Done-when line `DW<k>: ran <command> → <result>` or
+`DW<k>: not run — <reason>`; the findings R1..Rn (file:line, blocking or not); the verdict again
+last. Never post it: the script posts it and applies the label.
+```
+
+A further review, such as `/code-review <pr>` on an architecture task, runs only when the user asks
+for it and names the model (CLAUDE.md rule 6.2: one review unless the user asks for more); then
+always with the PR number, since a bare invocation from an agent reviews the wrong tree. (L8)
+
+
+# The review brief's own sections
+
+Every review brief carries these two sections, in full, after the numbered block of
+`process.md` §5 (or, in the review profile, after the brief's numbered lines). The reviewer reads
+the brief in another file, so paste them; never point to this one. Write "Blocking means" for the
+task; paste the second section as it is. (L47, L49)
+
+```text
+## Blocking means
+
+Any one is enough; a blocking finding means rework, never approve.
+1. A Done-when line fails, or cannot be run as written.
+2. What this task protects can be got past: <name it: the guard, check, permission, invariant,
+   rule value or file this task exists to protect>. A bypass you proved is blocking, even when it
+   looks like an edge case. Never "follow-up hardening" or "outside the threat model" unless the
+   task says so; if it does, quote the line. (L47)
+3. Behaviour the task forbids, or behaviour nobody asked for, inside a file the task requires. (L44)
+4. <project-specific items: a constant with no evidence, a test that passes with the behaviour
+   deleted, a status written into a document>
+Not blocking: wording, style, and defects in code the PR did not change: file those as follow-ups.
+When unsure, say how likely the problem is. Rate it blocking only if it is likely and would get
+past what the task protects; otherwise it is a follow-up. (L53)
+
+## Report every blocking finding in this one review
+
+This review is your only pass before the author fixes. Do not stop at the first blocking
+finding: finish reading the whole diff and the task file, check every Done-when line and
+every item under "Blocking means", and report all blocking findings together.
+
+- Before you write the verdict, make one last pass over the full diff for anything you have
+  not yet rated, and say "Final pass done" as the last line before the verdict.
+- Number the findings R1, R2, … in order of severity. A finding you held back because an
+  earlier one was already blocking is a review defect: if two problems share a cause, list
+  both and say so.
+- Do not rely on a later round. The author fixes everything you list, and the next review
+  checks those fixes and new code only, not anything you saw but did not report.
+- If you ran out of time or context before covering the whole diff, say which files or
+  sections you did not cover. Do not approve in that case.
+```
+
+Blocking means: likely violations of T34's determinism, integer geometry, no complete-game state, geographic constraints, provenance or tests that do not protect the implemented behavior. Give exact source lines and evidence; label unverified concerns. Final response must contain verdict, DW1/DW2/DW3, numbered findings, and final coverage limitations.
+
+Out of your depth: stop and hand back, with an ESCALATE block, when any of these happens:
+two hypotheses for the same question have failed; you would rely on bytes, code or behaviour
+you cannot explain; you are about to write a claim you cannot back with evidence; or you have
+made three attempts at one step without progress. Push your branch first. The ESCALATE block
+gives what you tried, the evidence so far, and the exact question you could not answer. Never
+guess a format or a cause.

--- docs/prototypes/new-game/T68/evidence/base-fixture/attempt-1/run.py	
+++ docs/prototypes/new-game/T68/evidence/base-fixture/attempt-1/run.py	
@@ -0,0 +1,17 @@
+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess,time,json,hashlib
+E=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+W=Path('/home/diego/projects/malpaco/.cache/agy-t34-review')
+argv=['/home/diego/.local/bin/agy','--model','claude-sonnet-5-5-high','--effort','high','--mode','plan','--output-format','stream-json','--print-timeout','12m','--log-file',str(E/'cli.log'),'--print',(E/'prompt.txt').read_text()]
+discovery=subprocess.run(['/home/diego/.local/bin/agy','models'],stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
+(E/'models.txt').write_bytes(discovery.stdout)
+assert discovery.returncode==0 and b'claude-sonnet-5-5-high' in discovery.stdout
+start=time.time()
+with (E/'output.jsonl').open('wb') as out:
+ try:
+  p=subprocess.run(argv,cwd=W,stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,stdout=out,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,timeout=900); code=p.returncode
+ except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+  code=124
+receipt={'model':'claude-sonnet-5-5-high','reviewed_commit':subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'],cwd=W,text=True).strip(),'exit_code':code,'duration_seconds':time.time()-start,'started_epoch':start,'mode':'plan','prompt_sha256':hashlib.sha256((E/'prompt.txt').read_bytes()).hexdigest(),'output_sha256':hashlib.sha256((E/'output.jsonl').read_bytes()).hexdigest()}
+(E/'receipt.json').write_text(json.dumps(receipt,indent=2)+'\n')
+print(json.dumps(receipt),flush=True)

from pathlib import Path
import hashlib,json,sys
E=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
if len(sys.argv)>1: E=Path(sys.argv[1])
assessment=json.loads((E/'assessment.json').read_text())
assert set(assessment['attempts'])=={'attempt-1','attempt-2','attempt-3'}
assert assessment['model_trial_urls'] and assessment['review_findings_relayed'] is True
for name in assessment['attempts']:
 p=E/name
 receipt=json.loads((p/'receipt.json').read_text())
 assert receipt['model']=='claude-sonnet-5-5-high'
 assert receipt['reviewed_commit']=='7f1860dac78932629340c561e8fae4cfcdf44589'
 assert isinstance(receipt['exit_code'],int) and receipt['duration_seconds']>0
 for file,key in [('prompt.txt','prompt_sha256'),('output.jsonl','output_sha256')]:
  assert hashlib.sha256((p/file).read_bytes()).hexdigest()==receipt[key], (name,file)
 assert receipt['model'] in (p/'models.txt').read_text()
 events=[json.loads(x) for x in (p/'output.jsonl').read_text().splitlines() if x.strip()]
 results=[v['result'] for v in events if v.get('event')=='result']
 assert len(results)==1
 result=results[0]
 note=assessment['attempts'][name]
 assert note['conversation_id']==result['conversation_id']
 assert note['denied_actions']==result.get('denied_actions',[])
 if result.get('denied_actions'): assert note['accepted_review'] is False
 if note['accepted_review']:
  assert receipt['exit_code']==0 and result['status']=='SUCCESS'
  assert not result.get('denied_actions')
  assert all(x in result['response'] for x in ['DW1','DW2','DW3'])
 if 'settings_restored' in receipt and not receipt['settings_restored']:
  cleanup=json.loads((p/'settings-cleanup.json').read_text())
  assert cleanup['temporary_grants_removed'] is True and cleanup['other_settings_preserved'] is True
 assert note['parent_assessment']
print('T68 receipts, discovery, output hashes and parent assessments verified')

display.text:
# Models: who implements, who reviews, and how

This page is the main session's working strategy for routing work to models, for
[isle-wars-archaeology](https://github.com/diegoami/isle-wars-archaeology) and
[malpaco](https://github.com/diegoami/malpaco), which share the harness.

- **One page, two copies.** The page is kept identical in both repositories as `docs/models.md`.
  A change goes to both in the same session.
- **No status.** The run-by-run record is the model-trials issues,
  [isle-wars-archaeology#9](https://github.com/diegoami/isle-wars-archaeology/issues/9) and
  [malpaco#3](https://github.com/diegoami/malpaco/issues/3).
- **The binding rules** are CLAUDE.md rules 1, 6 and 21. Where this page and those rules differ,
  the rules win, and this page gets fixed.

## Who does what (the owner, 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-12)

What worked in practice, after ten days of chains, pairs and quota checks:

| Role | Who | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Orchestrator | The main session, set by the Anthropic environment variables alone (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`): Claude; or GLM-5.3 through Z.AI's Anthropic-compatible endpoint, MiniMax, or Moonshot's Kimi when Claude's tokens are out | never named by the harness; its family is read from the environment (`lib/common.mjs` `sessionFamily`, `HARNESS_SESSION_FAMILY` overrides) |
| Implementer | The **`implementer` subagent** spawned inside Claude Code (worktree isolation) on a model of its own, not the orchestrator's: `sonnet` under Opus, which under Z.AI is GLM-5.3 Flash, or any model id the session's provider serves. **The main session** implements directly, in its own worktree, only where the provider cannot spawn a subagent. Asked before each implementation, `harness.json`'s `implementer.default` proposed first | `/run-task` step 2; `.claude/agents/implementer.md` |
| Reviewer | **One OpenCode run** of another family than the session's, on the model the user names at the question before the review, `harness.json`'s `reviewer.default` (GPT-5.6 Luna) proposed first; `gpt-6.1-sol` for a guard, a gate or hard research | `tools/harness/review.mjs [--reviewer <name>]`, as a systemd unit, watched |

The roster is the owner's and changes often: `harness.json`'s two defaults and its `blocked` list
change through `/switch-model`, never by a rule that names a model, and no quota, tier or
difficulty table picks one. The fixed rules: the reviewer is never of the session's family (so no
Claude reviewer under Claude, no GLM reviewer under Z.AI, unless the user asks for a same-family
review); a blocked model never runs (`--block`/`--unblock` change the list; it is empty today).

**OpenCode implements when the user dispatches it** (the owner lifted the ban on 2026-10-13):
T09 (PR #24) was implemented by DeepSeek via OpenCode on the owner's other computer, clean, from
the repository's own brief. The failure classes below remain what to guard against when briefing
an OpenCode implementer.

**Why OpenCode did not implement (2026-10-11 to 2026-10-13).** Its implementer runs were the harness's main source
of lost work: runs ended by a rejected path outside the worktree (T13 three times, T21 and T22,
mm-m3 on goal2's T29), by the reset between chain attempts, by a 900 s idle kill during a long
command, by a model ending early, and by models that did not follow the brief (`cd /abs &&`,
scratch files in `/tmp`, scope nobody asked for). The main session and Claude agents, which run
in the same tool with the same permissions as the session, had none of these failure classes;
their misses were review findings, fixed in a round. `implement.mjs`, the chooser, the quota
check and the chains were removed on 2026-10-11 (this repository's history before that commit
holds them).

**Why OpenCode still reviews.** A reviewer of another family catches what the author's family
misses (Sol's bypass findings on T06 and T08; Luna's citation checks on T02–T04, T10), and a
review is read-only, so a run that misbehaves costs one review, not a branch. OpenCode's models do
not always follow the brief: `review.mjs` reads what came back, posts a review it cannot read
whole under a note with no label (exit 4), and the main session reads it and decides rather than
paying for another. It gets the permissions a review needs in `.opencode/agents/reviewer.md` (isle-wars-archaeology: all
of `/tmp` and the static folder read-only; malpaco: `/tmp/opencode/*`), so a loose scratch file no
longer ends the run.

## The roster (`harness.json`)

| Name | Model and route | Family | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `luna` | GPT-5.6 Luna, `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, effort `high`, the direct OpenAI route | OpenAI | **the default reviewer** (L51): fast, proves findings by mutation |
| `gpt-6.1-sol` | GPT-6.1 Sol, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, effort `low` | OpenAI | the adversarial reviewer for a guard, a gate or hard research; `medium` only when the task file says why, never `high` (the owner, 2026-10-03) |
| `gpt-6-sol`, `luna-6` | GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna | OpenAI | registered for an explicit `--reviewer`; they share OpenAI's pool with Sol |
| `zai-glm-5.3` | GLM-5.3, `zai-coding-plan/glm-5.3`, effort `low` (no medium) | GLM | a credible heavy reviewer when OpenAI is out (T08 round 2); 3x in weekday peak from 8 Oct 2026 |
| `zai-glm-5.3-flash` | GLM-5.3 Flash, `zai-coding-plan/glm-5.3-flash`, effort `high` | GLM | a light reviewer for small PRs |
| `mimo-flash`, `mimo-pro` | MiMo v2.6 Flash and Pro on OpenCode Go, no variant (they offer none) | MiMo | a family of its own; Go needs `opencode console login` in the scripts' data directory |
| `mm-m3`, `mm-m2.7` | MiniMax-M3 (variant `thinking`) and M2.7 (no variant) | MiniMax | `mm-m3` registered here as the owner’s reviewer choice (2026-10-16); M2.7 remains upstream only; a family of its own; key `MINIMAX_API_KEY` from `~/.config/ai-keys.env`, never `opencode auth login` |
| `ali-qwen-max`, `ali-qwen-flash`, `ali-glm` | Qwen 3.8 Max (`low`), Qwen 3.8 Flash (`medium`) and GLM-5.3 (`low`) on the Alibaba Token Plan | Qwen, GLM | isle-wars-archaeology's `harness.json` only; register here through `/switch-model` when needed; key `ALIBABA_TOKEN_PLAN_API_KEY` the same way |
| (the session's provider) | the orchestrator's model from the Anthropic environment; `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable` or a model id for the `implementer` subagent, which the orchestrator spawns on a model of its own | Claude; GLM, MiniMax or Kimi when the environment says so | implements; reviews only when the user asks |

**DeepSeek was blocked** (the owner, 2026-10-09); **unblocked** (the owner, 2026-10-13, after its
clean T09 implement run): the `blocked` list is empty, and any model may implement or review,
subject only to the live checks — the reviewer is never of the session's family, and every id
comes from a live list (`opencode models <provider>`), never memory; `/switch-model` changes a
default with a probe, and `--block`/`--unblock` change the list.

**Effort.** A light model (Sonnet, GPT-5.6 Luna, GLM-5.3 Flash) runs at `high`; a heavy model
(Opus, GPT-6.1 Sol, GLM-5.3, MiMo v2.6 Pro, MiniMax-M3) at `medium` at most, and at `low` when
medium is not needed (the owner, 2026-10-05). A model that offers no medium takes its lowest
variant at or below `high`. Never `max`: slower, with no gain (L27). `--variant` on `review.mjs`
runs a registered model at another effort for one review.

**Sonnet's tripwire** (the owner, 2026-10-04). Models judge their own depth poorly. Every Sonnet
brief ends with this paragraph, and on an `ESCALATE` the main session answers the question itself
or takes the task over on the pushed branch:

```text
Out of your depth: stop and hand back, with an ESCALATE block, when any of these happens:
two hypotheses for the same question have failed; you would rely on bytes, code or behaviour
you cannot explain; you are about to write a claim you cannot back with evidence; or you have
made three attempts at one step without progress. Push your branch first. The ESCALATE block
gives what you tried, the evidence so far, and the exact question you could not answer. Never
guess a format or a cause.
```

**Beyond implementing and reviewing:** Jev (`jev-1.13` through OpenRouter) for repeated yes/no
decisions after a trial (`/jev`); OpenRouter models for images; ElevenLabs for audio. Their ids
come from live lists, never memory (`/delegate`).

parts.text:
All CLI logs mention the corresponding conversation_id. The CLI log ↔ output.jsonl correlation holds.

Now let me consolidate my analysis. Let me also verify the parent_assessment checks for evidence that the parent's interpretation is consistent with the retained outputs.

Attempt-1 assessment: "No review produced. Introductory text only; terminal command soft-denied despite exit 0/SUCCESS. Default request-review permissions require grants."
- Output: response="I'll start by reading CLAUDE.md and checking the tree state.\n" (61 chars)
- denied_actions: [{"action": "command", "display_name": "RunCommand"}]
- exit 0/SUCCESS ✓ matches
- "introductory text only" ✓ matches
- "terminal command soft-denied" ✓ matches

Attempt-2 assessment: "No review produced. Introductory text only; terminal command soft-denied despite exit 0/SUCCESS. Checkout hook loaded but did not supersede headless command approval; documented settings.allow grants required."
- response="I'll start with CLAUDE.md and the permitted Git commands. This is read-only work, so I'm skipping an implementation plan.\n" (122 chars)
- denied_actions: [{"action": "command", "display_name": "RunCommand"}]
- "Checkout hook loaded" → CLI log shows "loaded 1 named hooks from 1 hooks.json file(s)" ✓
- "did not supersede headless command approval" → CLI log shows "soft-denying tool confirmation" ✓

Attempt-3 assessment: "Valid supplemental review, NOT an approval: verdict rework. Focused10/10 passes; DW2/DW3, mutations and evidence audit not run. Full final relayed without omissions at PR150 comment6233951448."
- response is a 9592 char review with verdict "rework", R1 blocking, R2 needs owner decision
- DW1 is covered in the response (10/10 pass)
- DW2 is marked "not run" by Sonnet
- DW3 is marked "not run" by Sonnet
- review_findings_relayed: true
- model_trial_urls: 3 URLs (3 attempts)

Everything is consistent. Let me now finalize my findings.

Looking through this whole review, I see:
1. DW1 passes: verify.py validates the receipts
2. DW2 passes: git diff --check passes, harness-agy.md has all the required documentation
3. The verify.py rejects all the required mutations
4. The receipts are internally consistent
5. The CLI logs corroborate the narrative
6. The source-integrity.json hashes match the actual source files at 7f1860d
7. The prompts include Sonnet's tripwire in full
8. The parent_assessment properly does NOT claim approval despite exit 0

Let me consider any potential blocking issues:

**Blocking means (from the brief):**
- "T68 receipt verifier accepts missing/altered evidence or mistakes denied trial output for approval" - I proved verifier rejects all mutations
- "scope changes canonical harness/game or exposed credentials" - The diff only adds T68-owned files; no changes to canonical harness/game
- "actual trial is falsely represented" - The receipt claim matches the actual output.jsonl and CLI log

Let me look more carefully for any subtle issues:

1. The `permission.py` in attempt-2 is a Python script that would be triggered via stdin. The `hooks.json` configures a PreToolUse hook for `run_command`. The CLI log shows the hook WAS loaded. But did it actually receive the tool calls? Let me check more carefully.

Actually, looking at the narrative: "The first pilot stopped after introductory text; it is not an approval. The checkout-local PreToolUse hook loaded during attempt 2 but still did not authorize the command."

The run_command output shows the tool call duration_seconds:0.738416333 (under 1s for attempt-1) and 1.935848411 for git rev-parse HEAD in attempt-2. But the tool was reported as denied in the result event. So it seems the hook didn't grant - perhaps the hook triggered a denial or didn't override the default request-review permission.

Looking at the CLI log for attempt-2: "Print mode: soft-denying tool confirmation 'RunCommand' at step 3" — this suggests the hook did run (otherwise no soft-denial would happen), but its decision was to deny. Or maybe the hook ran but the overall default permission flow still denied.

Actually wait, let me re-read the hooks.json - it tries to run `t68-permission.py` (at .agents/t68-permission.py). And the permission.py returns {"decision":"allow" if cmd in allowed else "deny"}. So for `git rev-parse HEAD`, it should return allow. But the CLI log says soft-denied. This is consistent with the assessment: "Checkout hook loaded but did not supersede headless command approval".

Wait, but in attempt-2, the tools WERE actually executed (the run_command completed with output, duration 1.935848411). The denial only refers to "tool confirmation" being soft-denied. Hmm, this is a bit ambiguous.

Looking at attempt-2 output:
- step_update 2: view_file CLAUDE.md → DONE with output
- step_update 3: run_command "git rev-parse HEAD" → DONE with duration
- step_update 4: run_command "git status --short" → DONE with duration  
- step_update 5: run_command "git diff --stat ..." → DONE with duration
- final result: denied_actions: [{"action": "command", "display_name": "RunCommand"}]

So tools ran with output but the final result had denied_actions. This is consistent with the headless behavior described in the docs ("a denied command can still produce status: SUCCESS and process exit 0"). The hooks did execute, but the headless mode flags them as denied anyway. The docs note that hook can be ineffective.

This is consistent and not a bug.

2. Source integrity — let me also verify the witness-provenance.json is what the assessmentexpects.

# T34 supplemental review, PR #150 at 7f1860d (agy Sonnet)

This is a limited supplemental review. It does not approve the task, and it does not replace the MiniMax merge review.

**Verdict: rework.** R1 is blocking. R2 needs an owner decision.

**Tree proof**
- `git rev-parse HEAD` returned `7f1860dac78932629340c561e8fae4cfcdf44589`.

## Done-when

- **DW1:** ran `npx vitest run tests/core/island-geography.test.ts` → 1 file, **10/10 passed** (1.42 s).
  - Success checks cover only seeds 0, 1, 7, 42, 99 and 1994. "All exported successes" rests on the sweep, which I did not run.

- **DW2:** not run. `node docs/prototypes/new-game/T34/sweep.mjs` writes an evidence directory, and I was told not to write files.

- **DW3:** not run (`npm test`, `npm run build`, the pinned browser suites).
  - I have not verified the claimed 603 units and 24 browsers.
  - I have not verified that the e2e clock fix passes.

## Findings

**R1 (blocking, likely) — [island-geography.ts:217-221](file:///home/diego/projects/malpaco/.cache/agy-t34-review/src/core/island-geography.ts#L217-L221) and [the test, lines 10-13 and 31-33](file:///home/diego/projects/malpaco/.cache/agy-t34-review/tests/core/island-geography.test.ts#L10-L13): the retry, failure-history and exhaustion behaviour has no test that exercises it.**
- Retained evidence shows `failureCounts: {}` for seeds 0..99. Every seed succeeds on attempt 1, so `failures` is always empty.
- In the 10 tests, the `failures` loop at lines 12-13 appears never to run with real data. I am inferring this from the sweep evidence and did not rerun it.
- The only exhaustion test uses `attempts: 0`, which has no failure records.
